children: The Singapore dollar weakens slightly against its U.S. counterpart on a likely technical correction after touching a nearly four-month high late last week. "Into Monday, thin U.S. holiday liquidity and renewed geopolitical tensions may result in choppier price action," OCBC Group Research's Christopher Wong says. However, "unless the USD finds a fresh leg higher, upside in USDSGD may remain restrained," the FX strategist adds. The U.S. dollar is 0.1% higher at 1.2677 Singapore dollars; the greenback touched S$1.2655 last Thursday, the lowest intraday level since May 11, and fell as low as S$1.2656 last Friday, LSEG data show. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)
